findings.title: Server response
findings.action: No access error was observed in this request.
findings.explanation: The server returned a successful HTML response to our analyzer. This is the first step before extracting information.
findings.impact: This confirms access for our request, not for every official crawler. A status 200 alone does not verify that the page contains the expected content.
steps: Review the reading view to check that the expected page text was returned.
If an official crawler still fails, review hosting/CDN logs for that crawler rather than changing content blindly.
findings.where: Hosting/CDN response-header settings, server configuration or application middleware. We cannot inspect these private settings.

findings.title: Text in the initial HTML
findings.userTitle: Very little page text was extracted
findings.evidence: 25 words extracted from the main content.
findings.action: Check whether the important information is present before JavaScript runs.
findings.explanation: We read the initial HTML, without running JavaScript. Navigation, headers and footers are excluded from the main-text extraction.
findings.impact: Some tools may miss content that appears only after scripts or clicks. The 80-word threshold is a review heuristic, not an AI or Google requirement; a short page can be valid.
steps: Open Reading view and identify missing essential information.
Add real, useful descriptions as HTML text, rather than only images, canvas content or interaction-only sections.
If scripts generate the main content, ask your developer about server rendering or pre-rendering. Do not add filler just to reach a word count.

findings.title: Indexing directives
findings.evidence: No restrictions detected in meta robots or X-Robots-Tag.
findings.action: No change is needed based on the directives inspected.
findings.explanation: A noindex directive asks supported search engines not to index a page. nosnippet limits result snippets. A named agent rule may apply only to that agent.
findings.impact: These settings can limit eligibility in search experiences. They do not necessarily prevent a user-triggered tool from reading a public URL.
steps: Check the exact meta tag and/or HTTP header shown below, including the agent it targets.
If this page should be discoverable, ask the owner/developer to remove only unintended restrictions. Keep private, staging or intentionally excluded pages restricted.
Publish and then inspect indexing in your search-engine webmaster tools; this checker cannot confirm indexing.

findings.title: Title and description
findings.userTitle: Complete the page title or description
findings.action: Use a specific title and a short, accurate page summary.
findings.explanation: The title names the page. A meta description summarizes it and may be used as a search snippet. These are separate from the visible heading.
findings.impact: A missing description is a presentation opportunity, not proof that AI cannot understand your page or a requirement for AI citations.
steps: Write a unique title describing the actual page, not just your brand.
Add a useful summary of the actual content in the page SEO settings or <head>. Avoid invented claims.
findings.where: In your CMS: page content or SEO settings. In a custom website: the page template or shared layout. A public URL does not reveal which private source file generates this HTML. Look for the <head> metadata.
findings.verification: Publish the change, clear the relevant cache and analyze this exact URL again. Compare the new evidence with this report.
findings.example:
<title>Page topic | Your brand</title>
<meta name="description" content="A clear summary of this page’s actual content.">

findings.title: Main heading
findings.action: Prefer a descriptive main heading over generic labels such as “Home”.
findings.explanation: Headings organize what a page is about and make sections easier to navigate. We inspect heading elements, not their visual size.
findings.impact: “Home” gives little context about what you offer. Multiple H1s are not automatically an error, and heading counts do not determine AI visibility.
steps: Make the main heading describe the page’s real offer or topic.
Use section headings to group related information. Check the heading list below before changing your templates.

findings.title: Canonical URL
findings.userTitle: Check the preferred URL for this content
findings.action: Make sure the preferred URL matches the version you want search engines to consolidate.
findings.explanation: A canonical is a hint about the preferred version of duplicate or similar content. It is not a redirect.
findings.impact: A different canonical may be intentional. Missing canonical markup is not an AI-specific failure. We do not fetch or verify the canonical destination in this check.
steps: Compare the analyzed URL with the canonical value shown here.
If incorrect, update the SEO/canonical setting for this page. Do not force every page to point to the homepage.

findings.title: Extractable internal links
findings.userTitle: Review links to your other pages
findings.evidence: 0 unique internal destinations in the analyzed HTML, excluding the header and navigation.
findings.action: Link to relevant pages with descriptive, real HTML links.
findings.explanation: An <a href="…"> link provides a destination that tools can discover. A click handler without an href may not provide the same signal.
findings.impact: This count covers links in the remaining document after navigation/header/footer removal. It is not a site-wide crawl, and more links are not automatically better.
steps: Link naturally to related services, products or guides.
Ask your developer to use <a href> for navigation rather than only JavaScript click handlers.

findings.title: Structured data
findings.userTitle: Structured data is an optional improvement
findings.action: If useful for your page type, describe real entities consistently with the visible content.
findings.explanation: JSON-LD can describe a product, organization or article in a structured way. We check JSON syntax and list declared types only.
findings.impact: Valid JSON is not proof of a valid schema or eligibility for rich results. No special schema is required for Google AI features; absence is not a failure here.
steps: Review the affected <script type="application/ld+json"> block and its location.
If syntax is invalid, correct quotes, commas and brackets in the generating template or plugin.
Validate the appropriate schema separately and ensure its claims match visible content.

findings.title: Search crawler permissions
findings.userTitle: No search-crawler restriction found for this path
findings.evidence: No matching Disallow was found for the checked search agents.
findings.action: Choose which search agents you want to allow; keep training preferences separate.
findings.explanation: robots.txt declares path-specific crawling preferences. Search agents and training agents have different purposes.
findings.impact: A restriction may limit discovery by the affected search agent. An Allow rule does not guarantee indexing or citations. Allowing training is not required by this audit.
steps: Open the Crawlers tab and identify the exact restricted agent and rule.
Ask the site owner whether the restriction is intentional. If not, change only that agent/path rule. Do not replace the whole robots.txt with a generic example.
If rules permit access but crawling still fails, review CDN/firewall settings and verified crawler logs.
findings.where: Review the public /robots.txt resource or the robots settings in your CMS/CDN. It may be generated dynamically; we cannot identify its source file.
findings.verification: Publish the change, clear the relevant cache and analyze this exact URL again. Compare the new evidence with this report.

findings.title: Image text alternatives
findings.evidence: 0 images checked; 0 without an alt attribute.
findings.action: Describe meaningful images; keep alt="" for decorative images.
findings.explanation: Alt text offers a textual alternative for people and tools that cannot use an image. An empty alt can be correct for a decorative image.
findings.impact: We do not inspect image pixels or judge whether an image is decorative. Missing alt is a review opportunity, not proof that a vision-capable AI cannot interpret it.
steps: Review each image URL shown and decide whether it adds meaningful information.
Add concise alt text for informative images in your media editor/template. Put essential prices or service information in visible HTML text too.
